messages:
Maria G.: FYI seeing a slow but steady heap growth on long streaming sessions (tool-loop workloads). Repro: long chat + repeated tool calls for ~90m. Memory climbs ~1-1.5GB over baseline. Suspect KV pages not being reclaimed properly.
Tony L.: ugh. any flamegraphs or pprof yet? can you share minimal repro steps?
Maria G.: repro script attached (short):
```bash
# start a session that repeatedly calls toolchain, streaming tokens
python tools/long_tool_repro.py --iterations 120 --burst 20
pprof -alloc_space -png /tmp/profile > /tmp/alloc.png
```
I ran this on dev-infer-6 (a100s), attached sample pprof; flame shows hot on runtime::kv::page_holdcounts and runtime::evict_scan.
Kevin S.: link to flame: https://internal-grafana.local/flames/2955550000 (public not accessible) — from the trace I see a recurring pattern: candidate pages flagged for eviction get skipped because pin_count never drops to 0.
Anita R.: could be reuse pattern: small prefixes keep re-referencing same KV slab so coalescer never merges fragments; fragmentation increases and evict walker compensates but can't reclaim due to stale pin refs.
Maria G.: exact log lines:
```
I2026-03-12T15:22:10Z evict: found candidate page id=0x7f8a3 refcount=0 pinned=1 last_access=PT11m
I2026-03-12T15:22:11Z reclaim: scan skipped page id=0x7f8a3 because pin_count>0
```
This repeats for a set of ~120 pages that slowly accumulate and never drop.
Ben C.: did we change the kernel selector or batching heuristics recently? small token batches can change page residency and KV caching semantics.
Maria G.: we rolled kernel_selector=fastpath-2 in last week's runtime patch; also adjusted dynamic_batcher.max_batch=32 for tool loops. Reverting the kernel_selector in a dev build reduces the growth (observed in one run).
Tony L.: ok that narrows it. Can you try a build with the old selector + the new batcher? also try toggling per-session persistent KV cache (flag: --kv-persist=false).
Kevin S.: hypothesis: fastpath-2 enables an optimization that bypasses a refcount decrement on certain early exits from streaming tool calls. So some code paths never call page_unpin() if the response is short-circuited. I'll instrument page_unpin calls and add a histogram.
Anita R.: another angle: eviction waveback race. If eviction mark is set while a concurrent append to the same slab occurs, we could end up with a half-tombstoned page that stays pinned by background GC. Suggest capturing an allocation trace with jemalloc/heaptrack and also KV reference table dumps every 5s.
Maria G.: running a targeted dev build now with extra asserts (KV_DEBUG_REFCOUNTS=1). sample assert I hit:
```
E2026-03-12T16:01:02Z kv: assert refcount >= 0 failed for page 0x7f8a3 (ref= -1)
```
so we have a refcount underflow in some code path.
Ben C.: refcount underflow usually points to double-unpin or a missed pin. Which module touched that page last in the trace?
Kevin S.: stacktrace shows: runtime::streaming_exit -> runtime::tool_runner::short_circuit -> runtime::kv::page_release (missing a conditional guard in the fastpath kernel). Patch idea: ensure page_release only runs in the safe path or convert to RAII-style holder.
Maria G.: quick mitigation for prod: set kv.max_pinned_per_session=64 and kv.eviction_retry_ms=100 to be agressive on evict candidates. Also can disable fastpath-2 via runtime flag to stop regressions while we fix.
Tony L.: can we feature-flag the old behavior for Dedicated customers? we should avoid broad regressions.
Maria G.: yes, will push a rollback toggle: --kernel_selector=legacy if needed.
sre-bot: Incident created INC-2026-42: "Longstream heap growth due to KV refcount regression" and pager notified.
Kevin S.: next steps: 1) add instrumentation + tests for page pin/unpin, 2) repro in CI stress job 3) submit a small patch to guard page_release and add a regression test that runs long_tool_repro for 30m. I'll take ownership.
Anita R.: I'll help with jemalloc traces and build the KV dump ingestion to correlate page ids with client sessions.
Ben C.: also check quantization code path for any early-exit callbacks — we saw similar refcounty issues before in quantized kernel fast exits.
Maria G.: thanks team. I'll post the failing pprof and the assert logs to the incident. If anyone sees other strange pin logs grep for "pin_count" and "reclaim: scan skipped".
Tony L.: tagging infra: @oncall-infer to watch for spikes.
Maria G.: quick note: temp mitigation (confirmed on dev) using kernel_selector=legacy + kv.max_pinned_per_session=64 flattened the heap curve for a 2-hour run. We should ship rollback to prod next deploy if no side effects. :thumbsup:
Kevin S.: will open PR and link here when ready.
Maria G.: awesome — follow-up sync tomorrow 10:30 to validate CI run.
Ben C.: thanks all.
Maria G.: thanks :heart:
